name: Common Muffins
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: strong fresh yeast from the brewery
ingredients.originalText: two table-spoonfuls of strong fresh yeast from the brewery

instructions.text: Melt three table-spoonfuls of fresh butter in three pints of warm milk, set it away to cool
Beat three eggs as light as possible, and stir them gradually into the milk when it is quite cold; adding a tea-spoonful of salt
Stir in by degrees enough of sifted flour to make a batter as thick as you can conveniently beat it
Add two table-spoonfuls of strong fresh yeast from the brewery
Cover the batter and set it in a warm place to rise. It should be light in about three hours
Heat your griddle, grease it with some butter tied in a rag; grease your muffin rings round the inside, and set them on the griddle
Take some batter out of the pan with a ladle or a large spoon, pour it lightly into the rings, and bake the muffins of a light brown
When done, break or split them open with your fingers; butter them and send them to table hot

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Melt three table-spoonfuls of fresh butter in three pints of warm milk, set it away to cool
2. Beat three eggs as light as possible, and stir them gradually into the milk when it is quite cold; adding a tea-spoonful of salt
3. Stir in by degrees enough of sifted flour to make a batter as thick as you can conveniently beat it
4. Add two table-spoonfuls of strong fresh yeast from the brewery
5. Cover the batter and set it in a warm place to rise. It should be light in about three hours
6. Heat your griddle, grease it with some butter tied in a rag; grease your muffin rings round the inside, and set them on the griddle
7. Take some batter out of the pan with a ladle or a large spoon, pour it lightly into the rings, and bake the muffins of a light brown
8. When done, break or split them open with your fingers; butter them and send them to table hot
